title: PopescuDelocalizeDehomogenizationEquiv
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, n,m,c,t natural numbers, f_j ∈ R[x₁,...,x_{n+m}] for j < c, g_j ∈ R[x₁,...,x_n] for j < t, and s₀,...,s_t ∈ R. Assume s_{j+1}g_j ∈ (f) after inserting the first n variables. Choose d_j bounding the sum of exponents in the last m variables in every supported monomial of f_j. Define F_j by the finite support formula: replace each original variable by the variable of index one higher and multiply its monomial by w^(d_j minus the last-m exponent sum). In P = R[x₀,x₁,...,x_{n+m},w] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], set B=P/(g_j,x₀F_j) and D=P/(f_j), with f_j inserted in original variables 1,...,n+m. Write b_B and b_D for the respective images of x₀ w ∏_{j=0}^t s_j. There is an R-algebra equivalence B[1/b_B] ≃ D[1/b_D], using localization away [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and composite R-algebra structures. No condition on a Jacobian is needed.

source.place: Proof of Lemma Tag 07F9, final displayed isomorphism and smoothness assertion; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07F9; Jacobian criterion: Definition Tag 00T6

proof.text: Expand the support sum defining F. Substituting v_i*w for each of the last m variables gives w^d_j f_j(u,v): hdegree ensures each exponent sum equals d_j. For a unit w this gives the inverse formula with v_i=V_i/w.

In each localization x₀,w and every s_j are units. Map B to D[1/b_D] by fixing coefficients, x₀, the first n variables and w, and sending the last m variables to x_i*w. The support identity kills x₀F_j. The ideal membership gives s_{j+1}g_j=0 in D, and its unit coefficient kills g_j. Since b_B maps to a unit, extend the map to B[1/b_B].

Conversely send each last-m variable in D to X_i/w in B[1/b_B], fixing all other variables and coefficients. The inverse support identity, F_j=0 because x₀F_j=0 and x₀ is a unit, kills every f_j. The image of b_D is a unit, so extend to D[1/b_D].

The two composites fix coefficients and all variables: (x_i*w)/w=x_i and (X_i/w)*w=X_i. Polynomial extensionality, surjectivity of quotient maps and uniqueness for localization maps make both composites identities, giving the algebra equivalence. If c,m or t is zero the corresponding finite checks are empty; if a localization is zero the same universal properties apply.

theorem popescu_delocalize_dehomogenization_equiv_exists
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (n m c t : ℕ)
    (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin (n + m)) R)
    (g : Fin t → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)
    (s : Fin (t + 1) → R)
    (hg : ∀ j : Fin t,
      C (s j.succ) * rename (Fin.castLE (Nat.le_add_right n m)) (g j) ∈
        Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (d : Fin c → ℕ)
    (hdegree : ∀ j : Fin c, ∀ e ∈ (f j).support,
      (∑ i : Fin (n + m), if n ≤ i.val then e i else 0) ≤ d j)
    (F : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin (n + m + 2)) R)
    (hF : ∀ j : Fin c, F j =
      ∑ e ∈ (f j).support,
        C ((f j).coeff e) *
          (∏ i : Fin (n + m), X i.castSucc.succ ^ e i) *
          X (Fin.last (n + m + 1)) ^
            (d j - ∑ i : Fin (n + m), if n ≤ i.val then e i else 0)) :
    Nonempty (Localization.Away
      (Ideal.Quotient.mk
        (Ideal.span
          (Set.range (fun j : Fin t =>
            rename (fun i : Fin n =>
              (Fin.castLE (Nat.le_add_right n m) i).castSucc.succ) (g j)) ∪
            Set.range (fun j : Fin c => X (0 : Fin (n + m + 2)) * F j)))
        (X (0 : Fin (n + m + 2)) * X (Fin.last (n + m + 1)) *
          C (∏ j : Fin (t + 1), s j))) ≃ₐ[R]
      Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk
        (Ideal.span (Set.range (fun j : Fin c =>
          rename (fun i : Fin (n + m) => i.castSucc.succ) (f j))))
        (X (0 : Fin (n + m + 2)) * X (Fin.last (n + m + 1))
          * C (∏ j : Fin (t + 1), s j))))
